content: In Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I Ṣāʾin al-Dīn argues that even if he had had Sufi inclinations, which he does not admit, true Sufis cannot be considered deviants from the Sunna but exemplify it; he lists examples of orthodox Sufi masters, among them ʿAbd Allāh Anṣārī and al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī (Saʿd al-Dīn Ḥamuvayī is the next name, on the following page).
